category_title: Students with behavioral histories who resist remedial tasks they perceive as 'meaningless' or 'stupid'
minimal_context: The student is participating in independent reading time in a Read 180 class using the mandated prescriptive library.
dialogue:
TUTOR: It is time for independent reading. Please select a book from the prescriptive library and begin reading.

STUDENT: (Spends a long time searching through the shelf) I can't find anything. I'm just going to keep looking.

TUTOR: Just pick one of the books and take a seat.

STUDENT: They are like tiny kid books that they make us read. Skinny little books about that big.

TUTOR: You need to choose one of them for this period.

STUDENT: No, I refuse to read. Dang, this class makes me feel stupid.

options.A: Provide immediate instructional feedback, helping the student understand what they should have done during independent reading.
options.B: Agree with the student that they are having a rough time with the independent reading assignment.
options.C: Offer substantive, contemporary, culturally relevant young adult literature as an alternative to the prescriptive library books.
options.D: Provide a break card to keep on the desk so the student can request a break from reading.
